blocks.text:
Integrated A1 Communication
เป้าหมาย: ใช้ข้อมูลคน เวลา สถานที่ และคำขอร่วมกันในสถานการณ์เดียว

Use the language of integrated a1 communication to complete the unit's practical or interpretive task.
Identify and relay the essential information in the two readings without adding unsupported facts.
Respond to the two listening scripts with appropriate clarification and source-sensitive wording.

Reading A
Our class has a welcome day on Saturday. It starts at nine at the community centre. I am on the welcome team. I ask visitors their first names and give them name cards. The reading room is on the left. The café is next to it. A drink costs ten baht. At ten, we meet in the main room for a game. Visitors can ask us for help.

Read for purpose, then locate the people, events, conditions and limits. Read one short sentence at a time. Find names, numbers, places and times. Point to the words that answer a question. Ask for repetition instead of guessing.

Reading B
Welcome card: Saturday, 09:00–11:00. Community centre, Green Street. Bring a notebook. Water is free. Café drinks cost 10 baht. Reading room on the left; main room at the end of the hall. Use fictional visitor names during practice.

Compare the two inputs: what is shared, what is additional, and what is not known? Use only details actually supplied. All characters, organisations, figures and events in these inputs are fictional classroom materials.

integrating wh-questions
หน้าที่: ถามข้อมูลคน เวลา และที่
Model: What is your name? Where is the room?
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

at + time / place
หน้าที่: เชื่อมข้อมูลกิจกรรม
Model: It starts at nine at the community centre.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

can + verb
หน้าที่: เสนอความช่วยเหลือ
Model: We can help you.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

Guided practice: cover the word bank, reconstruct five target expressions, and explain their meaning in these particular contexts. Then use two in a new example. The same word may have a different sense elsewhere.

Listening script A — authored script; recorded audio and human audio QC are pending. Reading the transcript is text-based preparation, not evidence of independent listening ability.

A: Hello. My name is Lin.
B: Welcome, Lin. Here is your card.
A: Where is the reading room?
B: On the left.
A: What time is the game?
B: At ten in the main room.

Listening script B
Thank you for coming. Our game starts at ten. Please go to the main room. Bring your name card. After the game, you can read or visit the café. The welcome team can help you find the rooms.

First pass: identify purpose and main message. Second pass: note essential details and any corrections. Check against the script only after the listening attempt when approved audio becomes available. For now, practise with a teacher or partner reading the script.

Pronunciation and prosody
Keep the final sound of names and key words audible. Pause between ideas. Say numbers slowly and check them with a partner; intelligibility matters more than imitating an accent.

Interaction rehearsal: take both roles. Ask one clarification question, answer it using the source, and check that the other person has understood. Do not equate quietness, accent or hesitation with lack of ability.

Unit transfer task
ใช้ข้อมูลคน เวลา สถานที่ และคำขอร่วมกันในสถานการณ์เดียว

Prepare a 20–40-word response and a 30–45-second spoken response using the unit inputs. Exchange concrete personal and everyday information with support; isolated phrases may be sufficient where the task calls for them.

Planning sequence
1. Identify audience and purpose.
2. Select source details that the audience needs.
3. Mark any uncertainty, unconfirmed arrangement or missing information.
4. Choose two language features from Lesson 2.
5. Produce the response, then check meaning before surface accuracy.

Mediation: explain the essential information to a Thai-speaking classmate who has not read the sources. Preserve dates, quantities, conditions, agency and uncertainty. Say what cannot be concluded.

Online interaction: respond to a request for clarification, then add a follow-up checking question. Acknowledge corrections and revise your message where needed.

Quick review
integrating wh-questions: What is your name? Where is the room?
at + time / place: It starts at nine at the community centre.
can + verb: We can help you.

Self-check: Did I meet the purpose? Which source supports each factual detail? Did I make a suggestion sound confirmed? Can the other person act or understand appropriately? Which error should I revisit tomorrow?

rubric.descriptors:
Target A1: Exchange concrete personal and everyday information with support; isolated phrases may be sufficient where the task calls for them.
4 — Fully achieves the specified purpose with precise relevant detail, coherent organisation and effective control at this target level.
3 — Achieves the main purpose; minor omissions or language lapses do not materially distort meaning.
2 — Partially achieves the purpose; important detail, organisation or language needs revision.
1 — Limited assessable evidence; major gaps or distortion impede the task.
0 — No assessable response or wholly unrelated response.
Rate each dimension separately. For mediation, invented facts, erased conditions or reversed agency prevent a high fidelity score. Do not penalise an accent or a defensible alternative phrasing. Scores describe this task only, not certified CEFR attainment.

remediation.action: Return to Readings A/B; underline the evidence for your statement, restore any lost condition, and say explicitly what remains unknown. Retry Q-A1-16-015 and the mediation task.
